correctness.rationale: For one preselected port and distinct inputs, all permutations carry the same product of spatial amplitudes. Squaring the internal tensor symmetrization, normalized by 1/√(N!), leaves the Gram permanent. It is positive by testing against a tensor power of a vector having nonzero overlap with each internal input. Squared moduli of a complex Haar row are independent unit exponentials divided by their sum, so Dirichlet integration gives the Mellin formula and its first two logarithmic derivatives. For fixed t>−1 the gamma-ratio term in the scaled cumulant is ∫₀ᵗ[log m−ψ(m+Nu)]du. Using ψ(x)=log x+O(1/x) uniformly here gives −∫₀ᵗ log(1+u/α)du, zero at α=∞. At t=−1 the limiting cumulant diverges, and its right derivative tends to −∞ even for α=1. The effective domain has a neighborhood of zero, and the limiting cumulant is lower semicontinuous and essentially smooth, so Gärtner–Ellis gives a full good LDP. Strict positivity of F″ follows from ψ₁(1+t)>1/(1+t); its derivative at zero is −γ. Stirling gives Fα(t)=t log α−(α−1/2) log t+O(1) for finite α, proving infinite rate at and above the upper endpoint. Independently, expanding the exact log-Mellin transform at t=s/√N after subtracting the exact log mean yields (s²/2)[ψ₁(1)−Nψ₁(m)]+O_s(N⁻¹ᐟ²): the third derivative is O(N) there using ψ₂(x)=O(x⁻²) at large x and m≥N. This proves the asserted CLT including α=1 and ∞. Finally Z_N→F′α(0), and the arithmetic normalization contributes Fα(1). The stated gap is Fα(1)−F′α(0)>0 by strict convexity and Fα(0)=0. The internal-state factor cancels exactly. The uploader's finite Python check was inspected, not executed; it cannot establish the asymptotic claims.
residual_risks: The proof's claim of negative-moment divergence for every N needs the trivial m=N=1 exception, where P/κ=1; it does not affect the stated t>−1 identity or any asymptotic conclusion.
Fixed product internal inputs and one preselected port only; this does not give a fluctuation law for the union of all ports or for correlated input/interferometer preparations.

evidence: The Haar mean for arbitrary output subsets and more general internal states includes the fixed-port mean, but does not supply the log-probability rate.

Kaufmann–Thäle give stronger diagonal tail asymptotics with a prefactor and general p, but their statistic is invariant under radial rescaling. The proportional selected-row statistic retains the random selected mass. The logarithmic-spacing result inspected is Gaussian, not an LDP for that mass-corrected product.
The α=∞ cumulant follows from ordinary log-exponential Cramér theory, since the denominator's relative fluctuations are superexponentially small at speed N.
broader_coverage.reasoning: Neither a stronger mean theorem nor generality in p for a scale-invariant ratio gives the finite proportional correction. A targeted partial-coordinate search retrieved no stronger precise rate, which alone is not evidence of novelty.

evidence: Writing B=Σ_{i≤N}W_i and V_i=W_i/B decomposes Z_N into the same-coordinate log geometric/arithmetic ratio of V plus log((m/N)B). B is independent Beta(N,m−N) when m>N. Its tail at speed N cannot simply be dropped for finite proportional m/N.

A prior diagonal theorem plus a separate beta-mass LDP and contraction is another route. The closed finite-ratio cumulant has an explicit nonzero correction to the diagonal one; using the expectation to center the typical statistic gives Δα, not the minimizer of the uncentered diagonal rate.

originality.rationale: The distinct supported contribution is the explicit ratio-dependent law for a selected subset of a Haar row, in particular 1<α<∞, and the corresponding quantitative separation of the fixed-port optical probability from its own Haar average. The factorization and mean, the m=N large-deviation law in classical guise, and the dilute Cramér endpoint are not independent novelty. The strongest retrieved classical theorem concerns a geometric-to-arithmetic mean with the denominator taken over the same coordinates; it does not already include the fluctuating selected mass from the full row.
residual_risks: Bounded review; an unlocated classical result for logarithms of proportional subsets of simplex coordinates could further narrow the increment. The comparison is not a priority guarantee.

value.rationale: Fixed-port full bunching is a naturally measured optical event. The exact exponent distinguishes what a typical Haar interferometer does from what the familiar Haar expectation suggests, uniformly from dense to dilute scaling, and identifies when a geometric-mean approximation that drops the selected mass would give the wrong tail. The explicit finite-ratio rate and strict exponent, invariant under product-state distinguishability after normalization, are useful quantitative information beyond fitting a simulation, restating the mean or quoting the same-coordinate CLT.
residual_risks: No experimental sample-complexity bound or multiport union-event law follows from this review.
